headline: Phase I trial of trispecific T-cell engager clesitamig reports 20.8% response rate in SCLC
dek: Stephen V Liu summarised phase I data on clesitamig, noting cytokine release syndrome was manageable with step-up dosing but that anti-drug antibodies reduced drug exposure.
body:
A phase I study of clesitamig, a DLL3 x CD3 x 4-1BB trispecific T-cell engager, has been published in a journal tagged as @jitcancer, according to a post on X by thoracic oncologist Stephen V Liu.

Liu said cytokine release syndrome (CRS) occurred in 46.3% of patients. He wrote that with step-up dosing, all cases were grade 2 or lower.

In small cell lung cancer (SCLC), Liu reported a response rate of 20.8% and a duration of response of 4.4 months.

Liu also highlighted immunogenicity as an issue. He wrote that all patients developed anti-drug antibodies (ADAs), which reduced exposure to the drug.

The figures above come from Liu's summary of the study rather than from the full paper.
key_quote: immunogenicity an issue with all pts developing ADAs, which reduced exposure.
